coverage_notes:
TIERS RECOVERED IN FULL: head coach (1) and all nine on-field assistants permitted under the era's NCAA limit (Amato, Andrews, Burnham, Eason, Gladden, Heggins, Richt, Scott, Sexton); strength and conditioning (Van Halanger); four graduate assistants (Salva, Ragans, Morris, Stallworth); recruiting coordinator (Cottrell); the four football secretaries/administrative staff; seven medical staff; head equipment manager; and the video/academic support row.

SOURCE PATH AND WHAT EACH STEP YIELDED. (1) Wikipedia's 1993 team-season page has no coaching-staff section at all — its infobox documents only Bowden, Scott and Andrews, and the footer navbox adds only Amato and Richt with no roles. It was insufficient on its own. (2) NO archived FSU athletics staff directory exists near the title date. Florida State had no athletics website in fall 1993 / January 1994 (seminoles.com postdates this by years), so the Wayback Machine step of the plan is a genuine dead end for this season, not merely unsearched. (3) The 1993 Florida State Football Media Guide (200 pages) IS available on archive.org (item florida-state-football-1993-media-guide) and is the primary document behind most rows here. Its OCR is severely degraded: name and job-title lines are almost always split across separate lines, and many names are mangled ('Jack Marucei' for Marucci, 'Swe Hall' for Sue Hall, 'Cline Puri' for Clint Purvis, '18a Moris' for Bill Morris, 'Majo Billy Sith' for Major Billy Smith). Every quote I supply from that file was byte-verified against a fresh download of the _djvu.txt, but many are name-only fragments with the role explained in the accompanying note rather than contained in the quote itself. (4) nolefan.org's '1993 Football - Year In Review' page carries a clean, single-line 'Coaching Staff' roster that matches the media guide item-for-item; it is the best-formed source for the on-field staff and graduate assistants and is the only source I found for David Stallworth. It is a fan-run site, so I have paired it with the media guide or contemporary/official sources wherever possible. (5) Sports Illustrated's and 247Sports' 2023 30th-anniversary articles list 15 people under a 'Coaches and Staff' heading, which corroborates nine of the coaches and supplies Oravetz, Hall, Moore, Hogan, Wilson and Delegal.

WHAT I COULD NOT RECOVER. No analyst or quality-control tier is documented, and I believe none existed — those job categories postdate this era, and I found no such titles anywhere in the 1993 guide. No director of football operations existed either; Sue Hall as Bowden's administrative assistant is the closest analogue. Student managers, student trainers and student video crew are referenced generically in the guide but never named. The head athletic trainer's own bio page in the 1993 guide has its name header destroyed by OCR (it renders as 'Gavel leads astatoftes'), so Randy Oravetz's 1993 role is sourced from the FSU Athletics Hall of Fame bio (Director of Sports Medicine 1986-2010, 'directly responsible for the daily care and treatment of the football team') plus the anniversary honoree list, and cross-checked against the 1994 media guide which prints 'RANDY ORAVETZ / HEAD TRAINER' plainly. Three names on the 1993 support-staff photo page — Major Billy Smith, Pamela Eaves and Nick Menacop — appear with their caption line ('Taoey Deets, ‘om apa RetMeteane Beata') too degraded to read in either the 1993 or 1994 scan, so I have listed them with their titles explicitly marked unrecoverable rather than guessing. Clint Purvis appears in that same unreadable row; his 'Team Chaplain' title comes from a later Baptist Press profile, not from a 1993 document.

CAVEATS ON THREE ROWS. Dave Delegal, Wayne Hogan and Rob Wilson are included because the anniversary articles group them under 'Coaches and Staff' of the 1993 team, but their evidentiary footing is weaker than the rest: Delegal has no title in any 1993 source I could find (the equipment description comes from a 2008 seminoles.com article), and Hogan and Wilson held athletics-department communications jobs rather than football-team jobs — the 1993 guide's own media directory in fact assigns Wilson to basketball and lists Donna Turner as the football contact. A consumer building a strict on-staff-at-the-championship-game ring list may want to filter these three. Brad Scott took the South Carolina head coaching job for 1994 but coached Florida State through the Orange Bowl, so no mid-season departure applies; I found no documented mid-season arrivals or departures anywhere on this staff.

ONE PROCESS WARNING WORTH PASSING ALONG: partway through this research my local copy of the archive.org OCR file was silently replaced with the text of an unrelated 1993 University of Washington media guide, which briefly made it look as though the FSU archive item was contaminated. A clean re-download confirmed the archive.org URL serves 272,731 bytes of FSU-only content with zero Washington text, and all quotes above were re-verified against that clean copy. Nothing sourced from the corrupted intermediate state survived into this output, but if a later verification pass sees Washington content at that URL, it is a local artifact and not the source.
